RC2 — Ring underrun ⇒ FULL 150 ms re-prebuffer.
One late/lost packet = ~150 ms silence injected
at the source → hits EVERY output of the group.
airplay_source.rs:447-460

HTTP API / mDNS / discovery / other groups /
ALAC work (observed 100–294 ms; peak 873 ms) —
> the receiver's 250 ms lead ⇒ underrun = stutter.

RC5 — writer sink.send().await has NO pacing;
a full TCP window (WiFi radio power-save sleep)
backs up the 32-cap → drops. AP2 disables power-save
per-stream; do it host-wide.

div.div:
⚠ The ENTIRE end-to-end jitter tolerance for a sendspin output is the receiver's 250 ms lead.
Every hiccup above that budget — from ingest ring, non-RT relay, mutex, or socket — is audible.

div.div:
M4 — Fix the ingest ring (kills RC2 + RC3):
• on underrun insert only the missing samples (or a 1-quantum guard) and keep draining — do NOT reset to a full 150 ms prebuffer
• replace the hand-rolled ring + separate producer mainloop with a graph-clock-locked adaptive resampler (DLL / PipeWire rate-match), so the producer consumes at exactly the graph's pull rate and never drifts.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 550px; height: 1px; padding-top: 364px; margin-left: 1060px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
M1 — Realtime relay (kills RC1, the primary stutter cause):
do timeline.stamp() + mix + fan-out ON the sendspin-capture RT thread (it is already graph-clock paced), OR on a dedicated SCHED_FIFO relay thread (prio just below the capture / AP2 sender). Delete the unbounded capture→relay mpsc — no async hop between capture and the wire. General-purpose tokio work then can't preempt audio.

div.div:
M5 — Shrink the relay critical section (kills RC4):
encode/mix once; snapshot the member list, release the group + client_to_node locks BEFORE fanning out; reuse a preallocated mix buffer instead of a Vec per chunk.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 550px; height: 1px; padding-top: 586px; margin-left: 1060px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
M6 — Drop-to-live, never replay-late (addresses RC6):
when a member backlog is behind, skip forward to the newest chunk rather than sending the stale backlog (which arrives past the receiver deadline AND grows latency). Log every drop — today AP2 try_send and the 32-cap drop silently.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 550px; height: 1px; padding-top: 698px; margin-left: 1060px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
M2 — Real RT scheduling + isolation (backstop for RC1/RC5):
chrt SCHED_FIFO + CPU affinity — pin the PipeWire-RT, capture and relay/sender threads to dedicated cores; keep the tokio worker pool OFF those cores. Verify no priority inversion (chrt / ps -eLo rtprio). Disable WiFi power-save host-wide.

div.div: AirPlay-2 sender (Workstream A jitter) — same disease, mirror-image symptom

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 550px; height: 1px; padding-top: 925px; margin-left: 1060px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The final send IS an RT SCHED_FIFO thread with clock_nanosleep(TIMER_ABSTIME) ✓ — but its PRODUCER (run_streamer) is a NON-RT tokio task (= RC1) that, per 8 ms packet, does:
spawn_blocking(|| tx.send(msg)).await + yield_now().await
= TWO scheduler round-trips/packet (RC5b), feeding a crossbeam bounded(8) ≈ 64 ms channel. Under load the producer is scheduled late → the channel drains → 'Sender thread fell behind by 135–294 ms'.
Masked today by a 2 s AudioBuffer + ~1 s prefill + 1500 ms render delay — the OPPOSITE of near-realtime.
M3 — Fuse producer → RT sender thread: move ALAC encode + encrypt + prepare onto the sender thread; at each deadline it drains the (already RT-paced) capture channel, encodes, sends. Delete spawn_blocking + yield_now + the bounded(8) split. Then the render delay can fall toward network + one quantum.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 548px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1120px; margin-left: 1062px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: ROOT CAUSE (both paths): the timing-critical work sits on the shared general-purpose tokio runtime, decoupled from any realtime clock. Capture (PipeWire RT thread) and the AP2 final send (SCHED_FIFO thread) are correctly isolated — but the connective tissue between them (the sendspin relay / the AP2 producer) is not. Close that gap and the existing small buffers suffice.
